scope: Exploratory CPU, hybrid WebGPU, native Metal and browser SVG presentation on a shared desktop; not the release performance gate
order: Rotating and reversing CPU, GPU, SVG sample order
correctness: Exact CPU prepared reuse and integer CPU-span GPU composition must be byte-identical to fresh CPU output. F32 GPU coverage reports differential errors and repeat variation without an Exact conformance claim. SVG export bytes must repeat exactly; browser SVG pixel variation and accuracy ranges are reported without a deterministic-pixel claim.
render_time: CPU and hybrid build fresh pixels, including hybrid program/upload/completion/readback. SVG reuses one page export, its embedded image resources and decoded browser image, then performs fresh Canvas rasterization/readback.
frame_time: CPU/hybrid render including worker/WASI transport; retained SVG performs no worker export request after setup.
excluded_once: first GPU buffer allocation and packet validation
initial SVG export and embedded-image conversion
initial SVG validation, parse, image decode and first readback
required_separate_reporting: initial SVG setup and host cache hit
interactive_demo: Nine samples after two warmups; illustrative only
svg_slow_case_policy: An initial completed SVG raster exceeding 250 ms caps SVG at 3 timed samples and 1 warmup; CPU/hybrid keep the requested count. Actual counts and cap are reported. No slow input is silently excluded.
presentation: 12 samples after 2 warmups in top and centre 480px viewports. CPU/hybrid rebuild pixels; SVG reuses its exported page and decoded image. No forced full-page SVG readback. Request to two animation-frame opportunities, not scanout.
zoom: 18 fresh-resolution samples after 3 warmups across 1x, 1.5x and 2x, alternating top/centre viewport. SVG retains its vector image. A 60-frame CSS gesture uses the centre viewport. A path stops after a frame above 250 ms once at least 3 samples are collected, preserving earlier samples. A slow gesture stops after at least 3 frames. Actual counts are reported. Untimed accuracy readback samples the retained image and also compares it with fresh SVG serialization.
svg_cache_scope: One host export per current recorded page, reset on page/document change, bounded by 64 MiB. Encoded images are deduplicated inside that artifact. One parsed/decoded browser artifact per comparison, shared by all its samples. No application raster pixel cache.
coverage_experiment: Operations 5/6 export prepared geometry and exact exceptional cells. GPU integrates lines and true monotone quadratics in f32, then composites N16. Local mode subtracts an integer origin in f64 before narrowing. This is approximate and never advertised as Exact.
coverage_benchmark: 100 fresh exports/uploads/completed readbacks after 5 warmups; rotate/reverse native CPU vs local/absolute GPU and browser CPU vs exact-span GPU vs local/absolute coverage GPU. Same page-0 real PDFs at 72/150/300 DPI. CPU prepare and geometry export count; first adapter/pipeline/allocation/validation excluded and separately reported. Every sample completes a readback. Differential accuracy is checked outside timing.
coverage_limits: Existing opaque-solid RGB N16 admission remains; sampled paints, transparency and required F64 use explicit CPU fallback. Sparse winding/joint-clip corrections and clip classification stay in CPU preparation. Coverage work is moved, not the whole preparation stage.
retained_experiment: Compare Exact CPU PreparedScene reuse with retained expanded and shared GPU geometry. All paths rasterize fresh pixels on every redraw; no RGBA cache. CPU reuses its output Vec and Scratch; GPU reuses source/output/readback buffers. GPU warm samples make zero engine calls and zero uploads, verified by counters.
retained_scope: At most three requested resolutions per cache. CPU eviction uses the existing render_bytes reservation metric, capped at 256 MiB; this is not an RSS measurement and excludes separately bounded Store/output storage. GPU caches cap nominal source/output/readback buffer bytes at 256 MiB. Document/page changes invalidate retained resources.
retained_zoom: Twelve cold target updates with prepared/GPU caches cleared per mode/target; eighteen warmed updates after three warmups across 150/225/300 DPI. CPU and GPU retain the same three resolutions. New DPIs rebuild grid-dependent strokes/clips; cached revisits reuse preparation. Browser measures completed pixels/canvas upload/two RAF opportunities; native measures completed RGBA and separately IPC. Neither is scanout.
retained_control: Version 2 expanded geometry is retained as a control alongside version 3 source instancing and edge indirection. Setup order rotates by case; warm modes rotate/reverse. First setup is reported separately from 100 warm redraws after five warmups.
direct_display: Four rotating/reversing modes: CPU prepared reuse and fresh 480px Canvas/Metal viewport upload; retained GPU with RGBA readback and viewport upload control; retained GPU direct presentation; immutable world geometry plus per-view sparse CPU patches and direct presentation. All modes rasterize whole-page pixels each frame. Direct timed frames perform no RGBA readback or timestamp-query mapping. Diagnostic readbacks and attachment captures are separate.
direct_clocks: Browser request through two animation-frame opportunities; native request through completion and presentation-or-discard callback plus IPC. Native keeps every attempt and separate presented/dropped counts, with presented-only drawable duration. Eight-pixel native frame marker is outside the 480px PDF viewport. Neither clock is scanout and cross-host frame values are not directly comparable.
world_geometry: One canonical 300-DPI vector packet, retained/uploaded once per current document/page for integer views 72–300 DPI. Source-local edge rows and fixed conservative bins. One maximum-size reusable output buffer, at most three view-parameter buffers. No bitmap cache. Up to 64MiB geometry and 256MiB nominal GPU buffers; CPU view preparation/export and shared Store remain separately bounded. Nominal bytes are not RSS.
world_accuracy: Approximate coverage: sparse per-view exceptional cells remain CPU derived. Each new DPI still runs CPU preparation; warmed view hits make zero engine calls. Fixed-size annotations, device hairlines, adjusted strokes, zero-area fills/clips/shading bounds and active nonrectangular clips refuse world admission. CPU Exact is the differential reference; attachment equality is not a conformance or color-profile claim.
direct_zoom: Twelve genuinely novel DPIs [151,163,177,191,207,221,239,253,269,281,293,299], clearing prepared CPU reuse before each mode/target; then eighteen warm updates after three warmups across 150/225/300. Recorded scene, Store and pipelines stay warm. GPU geometry stays immutable across both studies. View-patch upload and CPU preparation costs count in novel frames. All readbacks for accuracy occur afterward.
integrated_host: A Swift application owns the native engine child and Metal. Bounded private MAP_SHARED files carry RGBA and geometry; safe Rust streams render_bands via std::io::Write. After one PDF upload on the input pipe, drawing uses 32-byte control requests and JSON-only responses capped at 16 KiB. No RGBA or geometry payload crosses the response pipe. CPU frame memory is wrapped by a Metal bytesNoCopy buffer. GPU work completes before any file is overwritten. No Node frame relay, Rust mapping, FFI, unsafe Rust or new product dependency. File writes still copy into kernel memory; this is not zero-copy rendering.
integrated_opening: 20 rotating/reversing document-cold opening trials per mode at 150 DPI. Each starts a native engine process/shared regions or browser worker/WASM compilation, opens identical already-read PDF bytes and waits for first presented frame/opportunities. The application, hardware adapter and presentation surface stay warm. Input file read/fetch and one application initialization are separate; do not label this application-cold latency or add medians into a claimed measurement.
integrated_redraw: 100 whole-page fresh redraws after five warmups at 72/150/300 DPI, rotating/reversing CPU prepared reuse, retained per-DPI GPU, and canonical world GPU. Native CPU streams bands into shared storage; browser CPU uploads full pixels into a retained Canvas. Geometry/pipelines/CPU preparation/output storage reuse are explicit. CPU fallback modes remain in the report.
integrated_scroll: 100 timed viewport updates after five warmups, rotating/reversing all modes on a retained 300-DPI full-page bitmap. Scroll changes only a 480px viewport. Zero engine calls, coverage dispatches and page-content uploads are verified between counter snapshots. CPU receives identical bitmap-cache reuse. Accuracy is checked later at top, middle and bottom offsets.
integrated_zoom: Twelve novel DPI targets from direct_zoom, rotating/reversing modes and clearing CPU prepared reuse before each mode/target. All preparation, export, shared writes or worker transfer, GPU setup/upload, rasterization and presentation are included. Scene/Store/pipelines stay warm. Median and p95 describe twelve different targets, not 100 repetitions of one target.
world_reciprocal: Opt-in --world-reciprocal computes a clip reciprocal once per mark/pixel, then multiplies each edge. Both hosts retain the original division shader as the default control. Coverage remains approximate, with unchanged admission and view preparation; this tests arithmetic cost rather than removing view-dependent topology.
demo_memory: Preparation follows the current 512 MiB product Limits default; the prepared LRU remains capped at 256 MiB charged bytes, Store at 64 MiB, wire/frame each 64 MiB. The experimental WASM worker has a separate 1 GiB aggregate cap for recorded/prepared/exported geometry and allocator high-water memory. The production browser host retains its 512 MiB aggregate default. These reservations and mappings are not RSS.
